regime.summary: Policy rate 7.0% on hold since the 2021-07-27 MPC. CPI has fallen from 10.84% to 8.34% in three months, which argues against a hike. The 6M bill at 7.49% sits only 0.49pp above policy, so no big move is priced. The rupee is weaker by 7.8% over 3 months and foreign corporates are net sellers, so I stay neutral, not risk-on.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 7.0%; last MPC decision 2021-07-27: hold (+0bp)
CPI YoY 8.34% for 2021-08 (published by 2021-09-03); three months earlier (2021-05) 10.84%
Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate +0.49pp (market near policy rate); CPI falling over 3 months (-2.5pp)

watch.subject: SBP MPC next decision
watch.trigger: Date of next MPC is not in the pack (calendar says see SBP calendar). Act only if the 6M bill cutoff moves clearly above 7.49% (hike risk) or CPI keeps falling with a hold (supportive).

watch.subject: KEL
watch.trigger: Latest EPS row shows eps_yoy 2.0 for the 2021-03-31 quarter while price is down over 3m. Revisit when the post-board-meeting result is public and price has not reacted; stale data, so no entry now.

watch.subject: AVN
watch.trigger: One upper lock, vol20/vol120 1.22, four material-info items, up 74% in 6m. Base rate says V4 is watch, not tradable; only revisit on a pullback that holds above its trailing stop.

watch.subject: DGKC
watch.trigger: 28% below its 252-day high, down 22% over 3m, with a material-information filing on 2021-09-10. Wait for the content of the filing and the first up close after a low; no hindsight-free rule exists.

watch.subject: MEBL
watch.trigger: At its 252-day high, up 26% in 1m, vol ratio 1.70, one upper lock. Extended; consider only after a pullback, and foreign selling in commercial banks must ease first.

watch.subject: THCCL
watch.trigger: Up 35% in 1m with vol20/vol120 2.48 and a material-information filing on 2021-09-03; extended and unexplained, so watch for the disclosure content before any view.

entries.reason: 252-day-high breakout in the leading sector (Tech & telecom, r6m +22.4%), with foreign buying of tech over 20 sessions. The base rate for breakouts is only a hypothesis (n=12) and the stock is up 32% in 1m, so size is small and the stop is a 12% trailing distance. Risk 1.8% of book.

not_known: No FX reserves or current account data, no IMF status, no valuation history, no consolidated EPS or balance sheets for most names, and the next MPC date is missing. The base rates are partly measured after this date and are rough odds only.
contamination_note: I used no knowledge of events after 2021-09-10. The base_rates.csv header warns its samples run past this date, so I treated those rows as rough odds for a type only and drew nothing from them about specific names.
